title: SLA-aligned model variant runway for Hosted API tiers
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Define and deliver a repeatable roadmap (runway) that maps Hosted API SLA tiers to curated model variants and rollout/playback policies. This ticket captures the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and execution plan to ensure customers receiving different SLA tiers (Free, Standard, Enterprise) are routed to appropriate model variants with clear performance/cost trade-offs and deterministic fallbacks.

Scope: 1) Variant mapping matrix by SLA tier (e.g., enterprise -> full precision large model, standard -> quantized variant, free -> smaller baseline model). 2) Routing and fallback policies (region-aware, capacity-aware, cost-safety). 3) Canary and staged rollout playbook per tenant cohort. 4) Observability: latency/cost/quality SLOs and alert thresholds wired to Console dashboards. 5) Eval guardrails and regression tests for each mapping. 6) Documentation & customer-facing comms for tier guarantees and expected behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: Variant mapping matrix published: for every SLA tier list primary and fallback model variants and quantization profile
Routing policy definitions checked into config repo and unit-tested (region, cost, latency fallbacks)
Canary playbook created and validated on two tenant cohorts with rollback steps and automated health checks
Console dashboard shows per-SLA token cost, P50/P95 latency, error-rate and quality-regression signal for the experiment cohorts
Documentation for support and sales (two-pager) published and linked to hosted API docs
Post-rollout smoke tests pass: no SLA tier observes >5% regression in quality metrics or >10% budget overrun within first 72h
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — alignment meeting with Eng (Priya), Runtime (Daniel), and Ops (Rafael). Agreed to prioritize Standard and Enterprise tiers for Q2 pilot.
2026-03-11: Trade-offs discussed: prefer using quantized variants for 'Standard' to hit cost targets; engineering flagged a potential latency tail with some quantized kernels under long sequences.

2026-03-12: Decision: implement per-route prefix cache pinning to mitigate tail variance for Standard tier during canary. Follow-up engineering spike (ENG-18421) to stabilize quantized kernel scheduling.
Design review (Marco): propose minimal UI to expose SLA tier and model mapping in Console route settings; engineering to prototype by M2.
Action items: add automated quality evaluations against existing prompt-suite (eval-suite/hosted-sla) before canaries; prepare customer comms draft for Enterprise early-adopters.
milestones: M2: Canary automation & route config checked-in (2026-04-05)
open_questions: What is the acceptable latency delta for Standard tier compared to Enterprise at P95? (proposed ceiling: 25% increase)
Should per-tenant cost budgets be auto-enforced by throttling or by notification and manual ops intervention?
Are there regulatory constraints for Private deployments that require an alternate mapping matrix?
retro_notes: To capture after pilot: include a short lessons-learned section and update the model catalog onboarding checklist with SLA mapping guidance
Plan a fallthrough test that intentionally exhausts Dedicated capacity to validate automatic fallback across regions
